messages:
emma: hi team - odd payroll/tax question. i was contracting through a UK vendor (paid GBP) until 2025-04-30, then hired direct US-FT on 2025-05-15. i just received a 1099-NEC in the mail for 2025 from the vendor addressed to me personally, but our payroll portal shows those months as vendor-paid. will that 1099 conflict with my W-2? also my last paystub shows a line 'withholding reconciliation pending'. any recourse?

noah (People Ops): thanks for flagging, @emma. can you confirm whether the vendor paid you as an individual or to a company entity? and did you submit any paperwork during conversion (W-9/UK tax docs)?

emma: vendor named me on the 1099 (weird) - i'll upload a photo to PAY-4447. i did sign a W-9 at conversion but not earlier. vendor payouts were in GBP to my personal bank. i assumed vendor would issue local forms in UK but got this 1099 instead.

julia (Payroll): @emma we've got PAY-4447. quick checklist: 1) 1099-NEC typically covers payments we didn't process as company payroll; 2) if vendor paid you directly and issued a 1099, that income is reportable on your US return regardless of vendor intent; 3) if our conversion included retroactive payment for contractor months, those retro wages would show on your W-2. We need to reconcile whether the company recorded retro wages for the same periods.

omar (Tax Counsel): tax context: receiving both a 1099 and W-2 for the same economic income can create duplication risk. If the vendor erroneously issued a 1099 for vendor payments already included in your W-2, we can request a corrected 1099 (1099-NEC void/corrected). Conversely, if the vendor legitimately paid you and we did not pay those same amounts, then it's solely 1099 income. Also note foreign-source payments paid while you physically worked abroad may have different sourcing; still, US citizens/residents report worldwide income.

emma: ok - what are next steps? worried about penalties if i file and both show up. also the 'withholding reconciliation pending' line worried me - is payroll going to withhold more?

julia (Payroll): action plan: 1) payroll will audit PAY-4447 and the GL to see if any retroactive employee payments were posted for Jan-Apr 2025. 2) if we find duplicates (we paid you and vendor also issued a 1099), we'll coordinate with the vendor to issue a corrected 1099 and we will ensure W-2 reflects the company's payments. 3) if vendor-paid income is separate, you'll get guidance on estimated payments/withholding. Regarding 'withholding reconciliation pending' - that's our internal flag indicating we may run a supplemental withholding if retro wages were posted without withholding or if we need to correct YTD withholdings. ETA: 3 business days. tagging @payroll-bot.

payroll-bot: PAY-4447 audit queued  assigned to julia  expected completion: 72 hours. :gear:

omar (Tax Counsel): interim advice: keep the vendor 1099 and any vendor payslips. if both forms remain, your CPA can attach an explanation and claim foreign tax credit or adjust for duplication. We can also prepare a company letter summarizing what amounts we included in payroll to help your filing.

noah (People Ops): thanks @emma for uploading docs. we'll follow up in-thread once payroll completes the audit. if you want a short call with Tax Counsel and payroll to walk through potential filing scenarios, we can schedule one.

emma: appreciate it - i'll hold funds aside until it's resolved and will attach the 1099 to PAY-4447. thanks for the quick triage. :pray:
